title.zh: 卷14 列傳第6 賀拔勝 弟岳 兄允 侯莫陳悅 念賢
title.en: Volume 14 Biographies 6: He Basheng (younger brother Yue, older brother Yong); Houmo Chenyue; Nian Xian
title.raw: 卷14 列傳第6 賀拔勝 弟岳 兄允 侯莫陳悅 念賢 Volume 14 Biographies 6: He Basheng (younger brother Yue, older brother Yong); Houmo Chenyue; Nian Xian

sentences.zh: 賀拔勝 弟岳 兄允 念賢

translations.literal: He Basheng; younger brother Yue; elder brother Yong; Nianxian
translations.idiomatic: He Basheng — younger brother He Bayue, elder brother He Bayong; Nian Xian

sentences.zh: 賀拔勝字破胡，神武尖山人也。

translations.literal: He Basheng, styled Pohu, was a native of Jianshan in Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: He Basheng, styled Pohu, came from Jianshan in Shenwu.

sentences.zh: 其先與魏氏同出陰山。

translations.literal: His ancestors, together with the Wei clan, came forth from Yinshan.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears shared a common origin with the Wei clan in the Yinshan range.

sentences.zh: 有如回者，魏初為大莫弗。

translations.literal: There was one named Ruhui, who in the early Wei served as Grand Mofu.
translations.idiomatic: One ancestor, Ruhui, served in the early Northern Wei as Grand Mofu.

sentences.zh: 祖爾頭，驍勇絕倫，以良家子鎮武川，因家焉。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ertou was unmatched in fierce bravery; as a good-household youth he was stationed at Wuchuan and settled his family there.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ertou was a warrior without peer; posted to Wuchuan as a soldier of good family, he made the town his home.

sentences.zh: 獻文時，茹茹數為寇，北邊患之。

translations.literal: During Emperor Xianwen's reign, the Rouran repeatedly raided as invaders; the northern frontier suffered from this.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xianwen, the Rouran raided again and again, and the northern border lived in fear of them.

sentences.zh: 爾頭將遊騎深入覘候，前後以八十數，悉知虜之倚伏。

translations.literal: Ertou led mobile cavalry deep in reconnaissance; on eighty-some occasions in all he fully knew the enemy's dispositions.
translations.idiomatic: Ertou led scouting cavalry deep into enemy country; on some eighty missions he mapped every move the barbarians made.

sentences.zh: 後雖有寇至，不能為害。

translations.literal: Later even when invaders came, they could not cause harm.
translations.idiomatic: After that, even when raiders appeared they could do no damage.

sentences.zh: 以功賜爵龍城侯。

translations.literal: For merit he was granted the title Marquis of Longcheng.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Longcheng.

sentences.zh: 父度拔，性果毅，為武川軍主。

translations.literal: His father Dubo was resolute and firm by nature and served as military commandant of Wuchuan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Dubo was bold and resolute and held the post of military commandant at Wuchuan.

sentences.zh: 魏正光末，沃野鎮人破六汗拔陵反，南侵城邑。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhenguang of Wei, the Woye garrison man Bolohen Baling rebelled and marched south attacking cities and towns.
translations.idiomatic: At the close of the Zhenguang era, Bolohen Baling of the Woye garrison rose in revolt and swept south against towns and cities.

sentences.zh: 懷朔鎮將楊鈞聞度拔名，召補統軍，配以一旅。

translations.literal: Huoshuo garrison commander Yang Jun heard of Dubo's reputation, summoned him to fill the post of commander, and assigned him one brigade.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jun, commander of Huoshuo garrison, had heard of Dubo's name and called him up as a regimental commander with a brigade under him.

sentences.zh: 其賊偽署王衛可孤徒黨尤盛，旣圍武川，又攻懷朔。

translations.literal: Among the rebels, the followers of the falsely appointed king Wei Ke'gu were especially numerous; they both besieged Wuchuan and also attacked Huoshuo.
translations.idiomatic: Of the rebel bands, the party of the self-proclaimed king Wei Ke'gu was the strongest; they besieged Wuchuan and also pressed Huoshuo.

sentences.zh: 勝少有志操，善騎射，北邊莫不推其膽略。

translations.literal: Sheng from youth had ambition and integrity, excelled at mounted archery; on the northern frontier none failed to esteem his courage and strategy.
translations.idiomatic: He Basheng had been ambitious and upright from boyhood and was skilled in horsemanship and archery; on the northern frontier everyone respected his daring and judgment.

sentences.zh: 時亦為軍主，從度拔鎮守。

translations.literal: At the time he too was a military commandant and followed Dubo in garrison defense.
translations.idiomatic: He too was then a garrison commandant and served under Dubo in the defense.

sentences.zh: 旣圍經年，而外援不至，勝乃慷慨白楊鈞曰：「城圍蹙迫，事等倒懸，請告急於大軍，乞師為援。

translations.literal: The siege had already lasted a year yet outside relief did not arrive; Sheng then spoke earnestly to Yang Jun, saying: "The siege presses tight; the situation is like hanging upside down. I ask to report urgently to the main army and beg troops as relief.
translations.idiomatic: The siege had dragged on for a year with no relief from outside. He Basheng then spoke urgently to Yang Jun: "The walls are closing in on us; we hang by a thread. Let me ride to the main army and beg for reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 」鈞許之。

translations.literal: " Jun consented.
translations.idiomatic: " Yang Jun agreed.

sentences.zh: 乃募勇敢少年十餘騎，夜伺隙潰圍而出。

translations.literal: He then recruited ten-odd mounted youths of courage and, waiting for an opening at night, broke through the encirclement and got out.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered a dozen bold young riders and, finding a gap in the lines one night, burst through the siege.

sentences.zh: 賊追及之。

translations.literal: The rebels caught up with them.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels overtook them.

sentences.zh: 勝曰：「我賀拔破胡也。

translations.literal: Sheng said: "I am He Basheng Pohu.
translations.idiomatic: He Basheng shouted: "I am He Basheng Pohu!

sentences.zh: 」賊不敢逼。

translations.literal: " The rebels did not dare press close.
translations.idiomatic: " The pursuers did not dare come near.

sentences.zh: 至朔州，白臨淮王元彧曰：「懷朔被圍，旦夕淪陷，士女延首，企望官軍。

translations.literal: Reaching Shuozhou, he reported to the Prince of Linhuai, Yuan Yu, saying: "Huoshuo is besieged and will fall at any moment; men and women crane their necks, looking to the government troops.
translations.idiomatic: At Shuozhou he appealed to the Prince of Linhuai, Yuan Yu: "Huoshuo is under siege and may fall at any hour. Men and women stretch their necks, waiting for the imperial army.

sentences.zh: 大王帝室藩維，與國休戚，受任征討，理宜唯敵是求，今乃頓兵不進，猶豫不決。

translations.literal: Your Highness is a pillar of the imperial clan; you share weal and woe with the state. Entrusted with campaign and suppression, you ought by right to seek only the enemy—yet now you halt your army and advance not, hesitating undecided.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness is a pillar of the imperial house; the realm's fortune is yours. Sent to suppress rebellion, you should seek out the enemy—yet your troops stand idle, wavering and unsure.

sentences.zh: 懷朔若陷，則武川隨亦危矣。

translations.literal: If Huoshuo falls, Wuchuan will immediately be in peril as well.
translations.idiomatic: If Huoshuo falls, Wuchuan will be lost next.

sentences.zh: 逆賊因茲，銳氣百倍，雖有韓、白之勇，良、平之謀，亦不能為大王用也。

translations.literal: The rebel band will thereby double their fighting spirit a hundredfold; even with the courage of Han Xin and Bai Qi and the stratagems of Zhang Liang and Chen Ping, they cannot be put to use by Your Highness.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels will take heart and fight twice as hard; even Han Xin and Bai Qi's valor and Zhang Liang and Chen Ping's counsel would avail Your Highness nothing.

sentences.zh: 」彧以勝辭義懇至，許以出師，還令報命。

translations.literal: " Yu, finding Sheng's words earnest in meaning, promised to march out, and sent him back to report.
translations.idiomatic: " Moved by the force of He Basheng's plea, Yuan Yu promised to march and sent him back with word of it.

sentences.zh: 勝復突圍而入，賊追之，射殺數人。

translations.literal: Sheng again broke through and entered; the rebels pursued him and he shot down several men.
translations.idiomatic: He Basheng broke back through the lines; the rebels pursued, and he shot several of them down.

sentences.zh: 至城下，大呼曰：「賀拔破胡與官軍至矣。

translations.literal: Reaching the wall, he shouted loudly: "He Basheng Pohu and the government army have arrived!
translations.idiomatic: At the wall he cried out: "He Basheng Pohu is here with the imperial army!

sentences.zh: 」城中乃開門納之。

translations.literal: " The city then opened its gate and admitted him.
translations.idiomatic: " The garrison opened the gate and let him in.

sentences.zh: 鈞復遣勝出覘武川，而武川已陷，勝乃馳還。

translations.literal: Jun again sent Sheng out to reconnoiter Wuchuan, but Wuchuan had already fallen; Sheng then galloped back.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jun sent him out again to scout Wuchuan, but Wuchuan had already fallen, and he rode back at once.

sentences.zh: 懷朔亦潰，勝父子遂為賊所虜。

translations.literal: Huoshuo also collapsed; Sheng and his father were then captured by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Huoshuo too gave way; He Basheng and his father were taken by the rebels.

sentences.zh: 後隨度拔與德皇帝合謀，率州里豪傑輿珍、念賢、乙弗庫根、尉遲真檀等，招集義勇，襲殺可孤。

translations.literal: Later, following Dubo, he joined in secret planning with Emperor De, leading local notables Yu Zhen, Nianxian, Yifu Kugen, Yuchi Zhentan, and others to gather righteous volunteers and make a surprise attack killing Ke'gu.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed Dubo in a secret plot with Emperor De (Yuwen Gong), rallying local leaders Yu Zhen, Nian Xian, Yifu Kugen, Yuchi Zhentan, and others to raise loyal volunteers and strike down Wei Ke'gu in a surprise attack.

sentences.zh: 朝廷嘉之，未及封賞，會度拔與鐵勒戰沒。

translations.literal: The court praised this, but before rewards could be granted, Dubo happened to die in battle with the Tiele.
translations.idiomatic: The court commended the deed, but before honors could be given Dubo fell fighting the Tiele.

sentences.zh: 孝昌中，追贈安遠將軍、肆州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Xiaochang era, posthumously awarded General Who Pacifies the Distance and Governor of Si Province.
translations.idiomatic: During Xiaochang he was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the Distance and governor of Si Province.

sentences.zh: 初，度拔殺可孤之後，令勝馳告朔州，未反而度拔已卒。

translations.literal: Initially, after Dubo killed Ke'gu, he had Sheng gallop to report at Shuozhou; before Sheng returned, Dubo had already died.
translations.idiomatic: After Dubo killed Ke'gu he sent He Basheng riding to Shuozhou with the news; before he could return, Dubo was dead.

sentences.zh: 刺史費穆奇勝才略，厚禮留之，遂委其事，常為遊騎。

translations.literal: Governor Fei Mu admired Sheng's talent and strategy, treated him with great courtesy and kept him, then entrusted affairs to him, regularly employing him as mobile cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Fei Mu admired He Basheng's ability, treated him generously, and kept him on; he put him in charge of affairs and regularly used him on cavalry raids.

sentences.zh: 于時廣陽王元深在五原，為破六汗賊所圍，晝夜攻戰。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Guangyang, Yuan Shen, was at Wuyuan, besieged by Bolohen rebels, fighting day and night.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Guangyang, Yuan Shen, was then at Wuyuan, hemmed in by Bolohen rebels and fighting day and night.

sentences.zh: 召勝為軍主。

translations.literal: He summoned Sheng as military commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He called He Basheng to serve as garrison commandant.

sentences.zh: 勝乃率募二百人，開東城門出戰，斬首百餘級。

translations.literal: Sheng then led two hundred recruited men, opened the east gate, and went out to battle, beheading over a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: He Basheng led two hundred volunteers out the east gate, fought, and took more than a hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 賊遂退軍數十里。

translations.literal: The rebels then withdrew their army several tens of li.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels pulled back several tens of li.

sentences.zh: 廣陽以賊稍卻，因拔軍向朔州，勝常為殿。

translations.literal: Guangyang, since the rebels had somewhat retreated, then withdrew the army toward Shuozhou; Sheng regularly served as rearguard.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy had slackened, Guangyang marched toward Shuozhou; He Basheng usually covered the retreat.

sentences.zh: 以功拜統軍，加伏波將軍。

translations.literal: For merit he was appointed commander and additionally made General Who Subdues Waves.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was made regimental commander and additionally General Who Subdues Waves.

sentences.zh: 又隸僕射元纂鎮恒州。

translations.literal: He was again attached to the Director of Affairs Yuan Zuan in garrison at Heng Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was again placed under Director of Affairs Yuan Zuan, garrisoning Heng Province.

sentences.zh: 時有鮮于阿胡擁朔州流民，南下為寇。

translations.literal: At the time Xianyu Ahu rallied displaced people of Shuozhou and marched south as raiders.
translations.idiomatic: Xianyu Ahu was then leading Shuozhou refugees south on plundering raids.

sentences.zh: 恒州城中人乃潛與謀，以城應之。

translations.literal: People within Heng Province city secretly plotted with them to surrender the city in response.
translations.idiomatic: Men inside Heng city secretly colluded with him to open the gates.

sentences.zh: 勝與兄允弟岳相失，南投肆州。

translations.literal: Sheng lost contact with his elder brother Yong and younger brother Yue and fled south to Si Province.
translations.idiomatic: He Basheng was separated from his elder brother He Bayong and younger brother He Bayue and fled south to Si Province.

sentences.zh: 允、岳投爾朱榮。

translations.literal: Yong and Yue went over to Erzhu Rong.
translations.idiomatic: He Bayong and He Bayue joined Erzhu Rong.

sentences.zh: 榮與肆州刺史尉慶賓構隙，引兵攻肆州。

translations.literal: Rong had a rift with Si Province Governor Wei Qingbin and led troops to attack Si Province.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Rong quarreled with Si Province governor Wei Qingbin and marched against Si Province.

sentences.zh: 肆州陷，榮得勝，大悅曰：「吾得卿兄弟，天下不足平也。」

translations.literal: Si Province fell; Rong got Sheng and said with great delight: "If I have you brothers, the realm is not hard to pacify."
translations.idiomatic: Si Province fell. Erzhu Rong gained He Basheng and said with delight: "With you brothers at my side, the realm will not long resist me."

sentences.zh: 勝委質事榮。

translations.literal: Sheng pledged himself and served Rong.
translations.idiomatic: He Basheng pledged his loyalty and entered Erzhu Rong's service.

sentences.zh: 時杜洛周阻兵幽、定，葛榮據有冀、瀛。

translations.literal: At the time Du Luozhou held armed force in You and Ding; Ge Rong held Ji and Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Du Luozhou then held arms in You and Ding; Ge Rong controlled Ji and Ying.

sentences.zh: 榮謂勝曰：「井陘險要，我之東門。

translations.literal: Rong said to Sheng: "Jingxing is strategically critical—our eastern gate.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Rong told him: "Jingxing is the key to the pass—our eastern gate.

sentences.zh: 意欲屈君鎮之，未知君意如何？

translations.literal: I intend to have you deign to garrison it—I do not know your mind on this?
translations.idiomatic: I mean to ask you to hold it. What do you say?

sentences.zh: 」勝曰：「少逢兵亂，險阻備嘗，每思效力，以報

translations.literal: " Sheng said: "From youth I have met with warfare; I have fully experienced peril and obstruction. I always think to exert myself, to repay
translations.idiomatic: " He Basheng replied: "I have known war since youth and every hardship of the field. I have long wished to serve, to repay
[variant: 已]

sentences.zh: 〔己〕知。

translations.literal: [己] know.
translations.idiomatic: your kindness.

sentences.zh: 今蒙驅使，實所願也。

translations.literal: Now receiving your command—it is truly what I wish.
translations.idiomatic: Now that you send me, it is exactly what I want.

sentences.zh: 」榮乃表勝為鎮遠將軍、別將，領步騎五千鎮井陘。

translations.literal: " Rong then memorialized Sheng as General Who Pacifies the Distance, separate commander, leading five thousand infantry and cavalry to garrison Jingxing.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Rong then memorialized He Basheng as General Who Pacifies the Distance and separate commander, with five thousand foot and horse to garrison Jingxing.

sentences.zh: 孝昌末，從榮入洛，以定策立孝莊帝功，封易陽縣伯，邑四百戶。

translations.literal: At the end of Xiaochang, following Rong into Luoyang, for the merit of settling the plan to enthroning Emperor Xiaozhuang, enfeoffed as Baron of Yiyang county, fief four hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Xiaochang he followed Erzhu Rong into Luoyang; for helping settle the plan to raise Emperor Xiaozhuang to the throne he was enfeoffed Baron of Yiyang with a fief of four hundred households.

sentences.zh: 累遷直合將軍、通直散騎常侍、平南將軍、光祿大夫、撫軍將軍。

translations.literal: He was successively promoted to Direct-Palace General, Regular Attendant in the Direct Office of the Secretariat, General Who Pacifies the South, Grand Master of Splendid Emolument, and General Who Calms the Army.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through Direct-Palace General, Regular Attendant in the Direct Office, General Who Pacifies the South, Grand Master of Splendid Emolument, and General Who Calms the Army.

sentences.zh: 從太宰元穆北征葛榮，為前鋒大都督。

translations.literal: Following Grand Preceptor Yuan Mu on northern campaign against Ge Rong, he served as grand commander of the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Grand Preceptor Yuan Mu on the northern campaign against Ge Rong as grand commander of the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 戰於滏口，大破之，虜獲數千人。

translations.literal: They fought at Fu mouth, routed the enemy utterly, and captured several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: At Fu mouth they smashed the enemy and took several thousand prisoners.

sentences.zh: 時洛周餘燼韓婁在薊城結聚，為遠近之害。

translations.literal: At the time Han Lou, ember of Du Luozhou's forces, gathered at Ji city and was a scourge near and far.
translations.idiomatic: Han Lou, a remnant of Du Luozhou's force, had gathered at Ji and plagued the country round about.

sentences.zh: 復以勝為大都督，鎮中山。

translations.literal: Sheng was again made grand commander and garrisoned at Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: He Basheng was again made grand commander and stationed at Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 婁素聞勝威名，竟不敢南寇。

translations.literal: Lou had long heard Sheng's formidable reputation and ultimately dared not raid south.
translations.idiomatic: Han Lou had long known He Basheng's name and in the end never dared march south.

sentences.zh: 元顥入洛陽，孝莊帝出居河內。

translations.literal: Yuan Hao entered Luoyang; Emperor Xiaozhuang went out to dwell at Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hao took Luoyang; Emperor Xiaozhuang withdrew to Henei.

sentences.zh: 榮徵勝為前軍大都督，領千騎與爾朱兆自硤石度，大破顥軍，擒其子領軍將軍冠受，及梁將陳思保等，遂前驅入洛。

translations.literal: Rong summoned Sheng as grand commander of the vanguard, leading a thousand cavalry with Erzhu Zhao to cross at Xiashi, routed Yuan Hao's army utterly, captured his son Staff-General Guanshou and Liang generals Chen Sibao and others, then advanced as vanguard into Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Rong called He Basheng as vanguard grand commander; with a thousand horse he and Erzhu Zhao crossed at Xiashi, broke Yuan Hao's army, captured his son the staff-general Guanshou and Liang generals including Chen Sibao, and drove on into Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 拜武衛將軍、金紫光祿大夫，增邑六百戶，進爵真定縣公，遷武衛將軍，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Appointed General of Martial Guard and Grand Master of Splendor with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon; fief increased by six hundred households; advanced in rank to Duke of Zhending county; transferred to General of Martial Guard and additionally made Regular Cavalier Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was made General of Martial Guard and Grand Master of Splendor with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon; his fief grew by six hundred households; he was advanced to Duke of Zhending and given Regular Cavalier Attendant as well.

sentences.zh: 及榮被誅，事起倉卒，勝復隨世隆于於河橋。

translations.literal: When Rong was executed, the affair arose in haste; Sheng again followed Shilong yu yu at Heqiao.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong was killed in the sudden upheaval, He Basheng again followed Erzhu Shilong at Heqiao.

sentences.zh: 勝以為臣無讐君之義，遂勒所部還都謁帝。

translations.literal: Sheng considered that as a subject one has no righteousness in avenging one's lord; he then led his command back to the capital to audience with the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He Basheng held that a subject owes no duty of vengeance to a fallen patron; he led his troops back to the capital to pay homage to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 大悅，以本官假驃騎大將軍、東征都督，率騎一千，會鄭先護討爾朱仲遠。

translations.literal: Greatly pleased, with his existing office he was provisionally made General of Cavalry on the Left and Eastern Campaign Commander-in-Chief, leading one thousand cavalry to join Zheng Xianhu in campaigning against Erzhu Zhongyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was overjoyed and, retaining his existing rank, provisionally made him General of Cavalry on the Left and eastern campaign commander-in-chief, with a thousand horse to join Zheng Xianhu against Erzhu Zhongyuan.

sentences.zh: 為先護所疑，置之營外，人馬未得休息。

translations.literal: He was suspected by Xianhu, placed outside the camp; men and horses got no rest.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xianhu distrusted him, kept him outside the camp, and gave neither men nor horses time to recover.

sentences.zh: 俄而仲遠兵至，與戰不利，乃降之。

translations.literal: Soon Zhongyuan's troops arrived; the battle went badly and he then surrendered to him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Erzhu Zhongyuan's force arrived; the fight went against them, and he surrendered.

sentences.zh: 復與爾朱氏同謀，立節閔帝。

translations.literal: Again joining in conspiracy with the Erzhu clan, they enthroned Emperor Jiemin.
translations.idiomatic: He again conspired with the Erzhu clan and helped set Emperor Jiemin on the throne.

sentences.zh: 以功拜右衛將軍，進車騎大將軍、儀同三司、左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: For merit appointed General of the Right Guard; advanced to Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Honorary Three Preceptorships, and Grand Master of Splendor of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was made General of the Right Guard, then advanced to Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Honorary Three Preceptorships, and Grand Master of Splendor of the Left.

sentences.zh: 齊神武懷貳，爾朱氏將討之。

translations.literal: Qi Shenwu harbored disloyal intent; the Erzhu clan were about to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan (Qi Shenwu) nursed rebellious designs, and the Erzhu clan prepared to move against him.

sentences.zh: 度律自洛陽引兵，兆起幷州，仲遠從滑臺，三帥會於鄴東。

translations.literal: Dulü led troops from Luoyang, Zhao raised forces from Bing Province, Zhongyuan came from Huatai—the three commanders met east of Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Dulü marched from Luoyang, Erzhu Zhao from Bing Province, and Erzhu Zhongyuan from Huatai; the three generals joined east of Ye.

sentences.zh: 時勝從度律。

translations.literal: At the time Sheng followed Dulü.
translations.idiomatic: He Basheng was then with Erzhu Dulü.

sentences.zh: 度律與兆不平。

translations.literal: Dulü and Zhao were at odds.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Dulü and Erzhu Zhao were at odds.

sentences.zh: 勝以臨敵構嫌，取敗之道，乃與斛斯椿詣兆營和解之，反為兆所執。

translations.literal: Sheng considered that nursing grudges on the eve of battle is the path to defeat; he then went with Husi Chun to Zhao's camp to reconcile them, but was instead seized by Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: He Basheng saw that mutual hatred before battle was the road to ruin; he went with Husi Chun to Erzhu Zhao's camp to make peace, but Zhao seized him instead.

sentences.zh: 度律大懼，遂引軍還。

translations.literal: Dulü was greatly afraid and then withdrew his army.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Dulü was terrified and pulled his army back.

sentences.zh: 兆將斬勝，數之曰：「爾殺可孤，罪一也；

translations.literal: Zhao was about to execute Sheng and reckoned his crimes: "You killed Ke'gu—crime one;
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Zhao was about to kill He Basheng and listed his offenses: "You killed Wei Ke'gu—that is the first crime;

sentences.zh: 天柱薨後，復不與世隆等俱來，而東征仲遠，罪二也。

translations.literal: After the Heavenly Pillar died, you again did not come together with Shilong and the others, but instead marched east against Zhongyuan—crime two.
translations.idiomatic: After the Heavenly Pillar fell you did not rally with Shilong and the rest, but marched east against Zhongyuan—that is the second.

sentences.zh: 我欲殺爾久矣，今復何言？

translations.literal: I have long wanted to kill you—what more have you to say now?
translations.idiomatic: I have wanted you dead for a long time. What have you to say now?

sentences.zh: 」勝曰：「可孤作逆，為國巨患，勝父子誅之，其功不小，反以為罪，天下未聞。

translations.literal: " Sheng said: "Ke'gu rose in rebellion and was a great calamity to the state. Sheng and his father executed him—the merit was no small thing; to treat it instead as a crime—the realm has not heard of such a thing.
translations.idiomatic: " He Basheng answered: "Wei Ke'gu rebelled and was a grave menace to the realm. My father and I killed him—a service, not a crime. The world has never heard such an accusation.

sentences.zh: 天柱被戮，以君誅臣，勝寧負朝廷？

translations.literal: The Heavenly Pillar was slain—when a lord executes a subject, would Sheng betray the court?
translations.idiomatic: The Heavenly Pillar was put to death. When a lord kills his minister, should I turn traitor to the throne?

sentences.zh: 今日之事，生死在王。

translations.literal: Today's affair—life and death lie with Your Highness.
translations.idiomatic: Today my life is in your hands.

sentences.zh: 但去賊密邇，骨肉構隙，自古迄今，未有不破亡者。

translations.literal: But the foe is close at hand; kin turn against kin—from antiquity to the present, none who did so failed to ruin and perish.
translations.idiomatic: But the enemy is near, and you turn on your own blood. From old times to now, such houses have never failed to fall.

sentences.zh: 勝不憚死，恐王失策。

translations.literal: Sheng does not fear death—I fear Your Highness will err in strategy.
translations.idiomatic: I do not fear death—I fear you will choose wrongly.

sentences.zh: 」兆乃捨之。

translations.literal: " Zhao then released him.
translations.idiomatic: " Erzhu Zhao let him go.

sentences.zh: 勝旣得免，行百餘里，方追及度律軍。

translations.literal: Sheng having escaped, traveled over a hundred li before he finally caught up with Dulü's army.
translations.idiomatic: Once free, He Basheng rode more than a hundred li before he overtook Erzhu Dulü's column.

sentences.zh: 齊神武旣克相州，兵威漸盛。

translations.literal: Qi Shenwu having captured Xiang Province, his military prestige gradually grew.
translations.idiomatic: After Gao Huan took Xiang Province his power steadily grew.

sentences.zh: 於是爾朱兆及天光、仲遠、度律等衆十餘萬，陣于韓陵。

translations.literal: Thereupon Erzhu Zhao together with Tiangguang, Zhongyuan, Dulü, and others—a host of over one hundred thousand—formed battle lines at Hanling.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Zhao, Tiangguang, Zhongyuan, Dulü, and the rest then drew up more than a hundred thousand men at Hanling.

sentences.zh: 兆率鐵騎陷陣，出齊神武之後，將乘其背而擊之。

translations.literal: Zhao led iron cavalry crashing through the formation, emerging behind Gao Huan's rear, intending to strike him from behind.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Zhao led iron cavalry through the line and came out behind Gao Huan, ready to hit him in the back.

sentences.zh: 度律惡兆之驕悍，懼其陵己，勒兵不肯進。

translations.literal: Dulü resented Zhao's arrogance and ferocity, feared he would override him, and marshaled his troops refusing to advance.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Dulü hated Erzhu Zhao's arrogance, feared being overshadowed, and held his men back.

sentences.zh: 勝以其攜貳，遂率麾下降于齊神武。

translations.literal: Sheng, seeing their mutual discord, then led his banners down in surrender to Qi Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing their split, He Basheng led his command over to Gao Huan.

sentences.zh: 度律軍以此先退，遂大敗。

translations.literal: Dulü's army for this reason withdrew first, and they were utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Dulü's wing broke first, and the Erzhu host was routed.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，以勝為領軍將軍，尋除侍中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taichang, Sheng was made General of the Palace Guard; soon removed as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taichang, He Basheng was made General of the Palace Guard and soon appointed palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝將圖齊神武，以勝弟岳擁衆關西，欲廣其勢援，乃拜勝為都督三荊、二郢、南襄、南雍七州諸軍事，進位驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、荊州刺史，加授南道大行臺尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu was about to scheme against Qi Shenwu; because Sheng's younger brother Yue held a host in the Pass-West region, wishing to expand his strength and support, he then appointed Sheng Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs of seven provinces (Three Jing, Two Ying, Southern Xiang, Southern Yong), advanced in rank to General of Cavalry on the Left, Honorary Three Preceptorships with an office, Governor of Jing Province, additionally granted Left Deputy Director of the Masters of Writing of the Southern Route Grand Camp.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu planned to move against Gao Huan; because He Basheng's younger brother He Bayue held troops in the west, he wanted to widen his support and made He Basheng commander-in-chief over seven provinces—Three Jing, Two Ying, Southern Xiang, and Southern Yong—promoted him to General of Cavalry on the Left with an office of Honorary Three Preceptorships, governor of Jing Province, and left deputy director of the Masters of Writing on the southern-route grand camp.

sentences.zh: 勝攻梁下溠戍，擒其戍主尹道珍等。

translations.literal: Sheng attacked the Liang garrison at Xiaxia, captured its garrison commander Yin Daozhen and others.
translations.idiomatic: He Basheng attacked the Liang fort at Xiaxia and captured its commander Yin Daozhen and others.

sentences.zh: 又使人誘動蠻王文道期，率其種落歸款。

translations.literal: Also sent men to entice and stir the Man chieftain Wen Daoqi to lead his tribes to submit.
translations.idiomatic: He Basheng also sent men to win over the Man chieftain Wen Daoqi, who led his tribes to surrender.

sentences.zh: 梁雍州刺史蕭續擊道期不利，漢南大駭。

translations.literal: Liang Yong Province inspector Xiao Xu attacked Daoqi unfavorably; south of the Han all were greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Yong Province inspector Xiao Xu attacked Daoqi and fared badly; the region south of the Han was thrown into alarm.

sentences.zh: 勝遣大都督獨孤信、軍司史寧。

translations.literal: Sheng dispatched Grand Commander Dugu Xin and army aide Shi Ning.
translations.idiomatic: He Basheng dispatched Grand Commander Dugu Xin and army aide Shi Ning.

sentences.zh: 歐陽酇城。

translations.literal: Ouyang and Zengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: They took Ouyang and Zengcheng.

sentences.zh: 南雍州刺史長孫亮、南荊州刺史李魔憐、大都督王元軌取久山、白洎，都督拔略昶、史仵龍取義城、均口，擒梁將莊思延，獲甲卒數千人。

translations.literal: South Yong Province inspector Changsun Liang, South Jing Province inspector Li Molian, and Grand Commander Wang Yuangui took Jiushan and Baizi; commanders Balü Chang and Shi Wulong took Yicheng and Junkou, captured Liang general Zhuang Siyan, and obtained several thousand armored soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: South Yong Province inspector Changsun Liang, South Jing Province inspector Li Molian, and Grand Commander Wang Yuangui took Jiushan and Baizi; commanders Balü Chang and Shi Wulong took Yicheng and Junkou, captured Liang general Zhuang Siyan, and seized several thousand armored troops.

sentences.zh: 攻馮翊、安定、

translations.literal: Attacked Fengyi and Anding, and
translations.idiomatic: They attacked Fengyi and Anding, and

translations.literal: (Feng)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: Feng]

sentences.zh: 〔沔〕陽，竝平之。

translations.literal: [Mian]yang, all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Mianyang, all were pacified.

sentences.zh: 勝軍於樊、鄧之間。

translations.literal: Sheng encamped between Fan and Deng.
translations.idiomatic: He Basheng encamped between Fan and Deng.

sentences.zh: 梁武勅續曰：「賀拔勝北間驍將，爾宜慎之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang ordered Xu: "He Basheng is a fierce general of the north—you should be cautious.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang ordered Xiao Xu: "He Basheng is a fierce northern general—you should be on your guard.

sentences.zh: 」續遂城守不敢出。

translations.literal: " Xu then held the city and dared not sally.
translations.idiomatic: " Xu then held the city and dared not come out.

sentences.zh: 尋進位中書令，增邑二千戶，進爵琅邪郡公。

translations.literal: Soon advanced to palace attendant, fief increased by two thousand households, advanced in rank to Duke of Langye commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Soon He Basheng was advanced to palace attendant; his fief was increased by two thousand households and he was advanced to Duke of Langye commandery.

sentences.zh: 續遣柳仲禮守穀城，勝攻之未拔。

translations.literal: Xu sent Liu Zhongli to hold Gucheng; Sheng attacked but did not capture it.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Xu sent Liu Zhongli to hold Gucheng; He Basheng attacked it but could not take it.

sentences.zh: 屬齊神武與帝有隙，詔勝引兵赴洛，至廣州，猶豫未進，而帝已西遷。

translations.literal: As Gao Huan and the emperor had a rift, an edict ordered Sheng to lead troops to Luoyang; reaching Guangzhou, he hesitated and did not advance, while the emperor had already moved west.
translations.idiomatic: As Gao Huan and the emperor had fallen out, an edict ordered He Basheng to lead troops to Luoyang; reaching Guangzhou, he hesitated and did not advance, while the emperor had already moved west.

sentences.zh: 勝還軍南陽，遣右丞

translations.literal: Sheng returned his army to Nanyang and sent Right Assistant
translations.idiomatic: He Basheng returned his army to Nanyang and sent Right Assistant

translations.literal: (Yang)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: Yang]

sentences.zh: 〔陽〕休之奉表入關，又令府長史元潁行州事。

translations.literal: [Yang] Xiuzhi to present a memorial entering the passes, and also ordered secretariat director Yuan Ying to administer province affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xiuzhi to present a memorial and enter the passes, and also ordered secretariat director Yuan Ying to administer provincial affairs.

sentences.zh: 勝自率所部，將西赴關中，進至淅陽，詔封勝太保、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: Sheng personally led his command, intending to go west to Guanzhong; advancing to Xiyang, an edict enfeoffed Sheng as Grand Preceptor and Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He Basheng personally led his command west toward Guanzhong; advancing to Xiyang, an edict enfeoffed him as Grand Preceptor and Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 時齊神武已陷潼關，屯軍華陰。

translations.literal: At the time Gao Huan had already taken Tong Pass and encamped at Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: By then Gao Huan had already taken Tong Pass and was encamped at Huayin.

sentences.zh: 勝乃還荊州。

translations.literal: Sheng then returned to Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He Basheng then returned to Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 州民鄧誕執元潁，北引侯景。

translations.literal: Province commoner Deng Dan seized Yuan Ying and brought Hou Jing from the north.
translations.idiomatic: A provincial commoner, Deng Dan, seized Yuan Ying and brought Hou Jing down from the north.

sentences.zh: 勝至，景逆擊之，勝軍不利，率麾下數百騎，南奔梁。

translations.literal: When Sheng arrived, Jing counterattacked; Sheng's army fared badly and he led several hundred horsemen of his staff south in flight to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: When He Basheng arrived, Hou Jing counterattacked; his army fared badly, and he led several hundred horsemen south in flight to Liang.

sentences.zh: 在江表三年，梁武帝遇之甚厚。

translations.literal: Three years south of the Yangtze, Emperor Wu of Liang treated him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: For three years south of the Yangtze, Emperor Wu of Liang treated him very generously.

sentences.zh: 勝常乞師北討齊神武，旣不果，乃求還。

translations.literal: Sheng often begged troops to campaign north against Gao Huan; when this did not succeed, he requested to return.
translations.idiomatic: He Basheng often begged for troops to campaign north against Gao Huan; when this failed, he asked to return.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝許之，親餞於南苑。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang permitted it and personally saw him off at Southern Park.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang agreed and personally saw him off at Southern Park.

sentences.zh: 勝自是之後，每行執弓矢，見鳥獸南向者皆不射之，以申懷德之志也。

translations.literal: From then on, whenever Sheng traveled with bow and arrows, he would not shoot at birds or beasts facing south, to express his grateful heart.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, whenever He Basheng went out with bow and arrows, he would not shoot birds or beasts facing south, to show his gratitude.

sentences.zh: 旣至長安，詣闕謝罪。

translations.literal: Having reached Chang'an, he went to the palace to apologize.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Chang'an, he went to the palace to apologize.

sentences.zh: 朝廷嘉其還，乃授太師。

translations.literal: The court praised his return and appointed him Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: The court praised his return and appointed him Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 後從太祖擒竇泰于小關，加授中軍大都督。

translations.literal: Later he followed the Grand Progenitor in capturing Dou Tai at Xiaoguan and was additionally appointed Grand Commander of the Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai in capturing Dou Tai at Xiaoguan and was additionally appointed Grand Commander of the Central Army.

sentences.zh: 又從太祖攻弘農。

translations.literal: He also followed the Grand Progenitor in attacking Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: He also followed Yuwen Tai in attacking Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 勝自陝津先渡河，東魏將高干遁，勝追獲，囚之。

translations.literal: Sheng crossed the river first from Shan crossing; Eastern Wei general Gao Gan fled; Sheng pursued and captured him and imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: He Basheng crossed the river first from Shan crossing; Eastern Wei general Gao Gan fled, but He Basheng pursued, captured, and imprisoned him.

sentences.zh: 下河北，擒郡守孫晏。

translations.literal: Going down north of the river, he captured commandery administrator Sun Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He went down north of the river and captured commandery administrator Sun Yan.

sentences.zh: 崔乂。

translations.literal: Cui Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He also captured Cui Yi.

sentences.zh: 從破東魏軍於沙苑，追奔至河上。

translations.literal: He followed in defeating Eastern Wei armies at Shawei and pursued the fugitives to the river bank.
translations.idiomatic: He followed in defeating Eastern Wei armies at Shawei and pursued the fugitives to the riverbank.

sentences.zh: 仍與李弼別攻河東，略定汾、絳。

translations.literal: Still with Li Bi he separately attacked Hedong and pacified Fen and Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined Li Bi in a separate attack on Hedong and pacified Fen and Jiang.

sentences.zh: 增邑幷前五千戶。

translations.literal: Fief increased together with previous to five thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: His fief was increased together with the previous total to five thousand households.

sentences.zh: 河橋之役，勝大破東魏軍。

translations.literal: In the campaign at Heqiao, Sheng greatly defeated Eastern Wei armies.
translations.idiomatic: At the battle of Heqiao, He Basheng routed the Eastern Wei army.

sentences.zh: 太祖命勝收其降卒而還。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor ordered Sheng to gather the surrendered troops and return.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai ordered He Basheng to gather the surrendered troops and return.

sentences.zh: 及齊神武悉衆攻玉壁，勝以前軍大都督從太祖追之於汾北。

translations.literal: When Gao Huan mobilized all forces to attack Yubi, Sheng as vanguard grand commander followed the Grand Progenitor in pursuing him on the north bank of the Fen.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan mobilized all his forces to attack Yubi, He Basheng as vanguard grand commander followed Yuwen Tai in pursuing him on the north bank of the Fen.

sentences.zh: 又從戰邙山。

translations.literal: He also followed in fighting at Mount Mang.
translations.idiomatic: He also fought at Mount Mang.

sentences.zh: 時太祖見齊神武旗鼓，識之，乃募敢勇三千人，配勝以犯其軍。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor saw Gao Huan's banners and drums and recognized him, he recruited three thousand brave men and assigned them to Sheng to strike his army.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Tai saw Gao Huan's banners and drums and recognized him, he recruited three thousand brave men and assigned them to He Basheng to strike his army.

sentences.zh: 勝適與齊神武相遇，因告之曰：「賀六渾，賀拔破胡必殺汝也。

translations.literal: Sheng happened to meet Gao Huan and thus told him: "He Liu Hun—He Basheng He Pohu will surely kill you!
translations.idiomatic: He Basheng happened to meet Gao Huan and shouted: "He Liu Hun—He Basheng He Pohu will kill you!

sentences.zh: 」時募士皆用短兵接戰，勝持矟追齊神武數里，刃垂及之。

translations.literal: " At the time the recruited warriors all fought with short weapons at close quarters; Sheng held a spear and chased Gao Huan several li, the blade nearly reaching him.
translations.idiomatic: " The recruited warriors all fought hand to hand with short weapons; He Basheng held a spear and chased Gao Huan for several li, the blade nearly reaching him.

sentences.zh: 會勝馬為流矢所中，死，比副騎至，齊神武已逸去。

translations.literal: As it happened Sheng's horse was struck by a stray arrow and died; by the time his escort riders arrived, Gao Huan had already escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Just then He Basheng's horse was struck by a stray arrow and died; by the time his escort caught up, Gao Huan had already escaped.

sentences.zh: 勝歎曰：「今日之事，吾不執弓矢者，天也！」

translations.literal: Sheng sighed: "In today's affair, that I did not have bow and arrows in hand—that was Heaven!"
translations.idiomatic: He Basheng sighed: "In today's affair, that I had no bow and arrows in hand—that was Heaven!"

sentences.zh: 勝長於喪亂之中，尤工武藝，走馬射飛鳥，十中其五六。

translations.literal: Sheng grew up amid turmoil and was especially skilled in martial arts; riding at a gallop he shot flying birds and hit five or six of ten.
translations.idiomatic: He Basheng grew up amid turmoil and was especially skilled in martial arts; riding at a gallop he shot flying birds and hit five or six out of ten.

sentences.zh: 太祖每云：「諸將對敵，神色皆動，唯賀拔公臨陣如平常，真大勇也。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor often said: "When the generals face the enemy their expressions all change—only Duke Heba at battle is as in ordinary times; true great courage.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai often said: "When the generals face the enemy their expressions all change—only Lord He Basheng at battle is as at ordinary times; that is true great courage.

sentences.zh: 」自居重位，始愛墳籍。

translations.literal: " From taking a weighty position, he began to love books and records.
translations.idiomatic: " Once he held high rank, he began to love books and records.

sentences.zh: 乃招引文儒，討論義理。

translations.literal: He then invited literati and Confucians to discuss principles.
translations.idiomatic: He invited literati and Confucians to discuss principles.

sentences.zh: 性又通率，重義輕財，身死之日，唯有隨身兵仗及書千餘卷而已。

translations.literal: By nature he was also straightforward and unadorned, valuing righteousness and slighting wealth; on the day of his death he had only personal weapons and more than a thousand scrolls of books.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was straightforward and unadorned, valuing righteousness over wealth; when he died he had only his personal weapons and more than a thousand scrolls of books.

sentences.zh: 初，勝至關中，自以年位素重，見太祖不拜，尋而自悔，太祖亦有望焉。

translations.literal: Initially when Sheng reached Guanzhong, deeming his years and rank always weighty, he did not bow on seeing the Grand Progenitor; soon he regretted it himself, and the Grand Progenitor also had expectations regarding this.
translations.idiomatic: When He Basheng first reached Guanzhong, thinking his years and rank entitled him, he did not bow to Yuwen Tai; soon he regretted it, and Yuwen Tai also had expectations in the matter.

sentences.zh: 後從太祖宴于昆明池，時有雙鳧游于池上，太祖乃授弓矢於勝曰：「不見公射久矣，請以為歡。

translations.literal: Later following the Grand Progenitor at a banquet at Kunming Pond, when a pair of wild ducks swam on the pond, the Grand Progenitor handed bow and arrows to Sheng and said: "It has been long since we have seen you shoot—please take this for amusement.
translations.idiomatic: Later, at a banquet with Yuwen Tai at Kunming Pond, when a pair of wild ducks swam on the pond, Yuwen Tai handed bow and arrows to He Basheng and said: "It has been long since we have seen you shoot—please do so for our pleasure.

sentences.zh: 」勝射之，一發俱中。

translations.literal: " Sheng shot them; one volley hit both.
translations.idiomatic: " He Basheng shot; one volley brought down both.

sentences.zh: 因拜太祖曰：「使勝得奉神武，以討不庭，皆如此也。

translations.literal: He then bowed to the Grand Progenitor and said: "If Sheng could serve in martial endeavor to punish the unsubmissive, all would be like this.
translations.idiomatic: He then bowed to Yuwen Tai and said: "If I could serve you in arms to punish the rebellious, every shot would be like this.

sentences.zh: 」太祖大悅。

translations.literal: " The Grand Progenitor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuwen Tai was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 自是恩禮日重，勝亦盡誠推奉焉。

translations.literal: From then favor and courtesy daily grew heavier, and Sheng also devoted himself fully in loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: From then favor and courtesy grew daily, and He Basheng also devoted himself fully in loyalty.

sentences.zh: 贈定冀等十州諸軍事、定州刺史、太宰、錄尚書事，諡曰貞獻。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Director of military affairs for Ding, Ji, and ten other provinces, Inspector of Ding Province, Grand Preceptor, and Director of the Masters of Writing; posthumous title Loyal Offerer.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Director of military affairs for Ding, Ji, and ten other provinces, Inspector of Ding Province, Grand Preceptor, and Director of the Masters of Writing, with the posthumous title Loyal Offerer.

sentences.zh: 明帝二年，以勝配享太祖廟庭。

translations.literal: In the second year of Emperor Ming, Sheng was paired to share offerings in the Grand Progenitor's temple court.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Emperor Ming (558), He Basheng was paired to share offerings in Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai's temple court.

sentences.zh: 勝無子，以弟岳子仲華嗣。

translations.literal: Sheng had no sons; his younger brother Bayue's son Zhonghua succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He Basheng had no sons; his younger brother He Bayue's son Zhonghua succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 大統三年，賜爵樊城公。

translations.literal: In the third year of Datong, he was granted the rank of Duke of Fancheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Datong (537), he was granted the rank of Duke of Fancheng.

sentences.zh: 魏廢帝時，為通直郎、散騎常侍，遷黃門郎，加車騎大將軍、儀同三司，驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: During the Deposed Emperor of Wei era, he served as direct-attendant gentleman, scattered-cavalry regular attendant; transferred to Yellow Gate Gentleman; added Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Commissioner with Three Excellencies protocol, Flying-cavalry Grand General and Grand Master of Magnificent State with Three Excellencies protocol.
translations.idiomatic: During the era of the Deposed Emperor of Wei, he served as direct-attendant gentleman and scattered-cavalry regular attendant, was transferred to Yellow Gate Gentleman, and was given Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry with Commissioner of Three Excellencies protocol, then Flying-cavalry Grand General with Grand Master of Magnificent State and Three Excellencies protocol.

sentences.zh: 六官建，拜守廟下大夫。

translations.literal: When the Six Offices were established, appointed Gentleman under the Temple Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: When the Six Offices were established, he was appointed Gentleman under the Temple Guardian.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，襲爵琅邪公，除利州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin ascended the throne, he inherited the rank of Duke of Langye and was appointed Inspector of Li Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin ascended the throne, he inherited the rank of Duke of Langye and was appointed Inspector of Li Province.

sentences.zh: 大象末，位至江陵總管。

translations.literal: At the end of Daxiang, he reached the position of Overall Manager of Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Daxiang (581), he reached the position of Overall Manager of Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 勝兄弟三人，竝以豪俠知名。

translations.literal: The three He brothers were all famed as heroic knights.
translations.idiomatic: The three He brothers were all famed as heroic knights.

sentences.zh: 兄允字阿泥，魏孝武時，位至太尉，封燕郡王，為神武所害。

translations.literal: Older brother Yong, styled Ani; during Emperor Xiaowu of Wei, reached Grand Commandant, enfeoffed Prince of Yan commandery; was killed by Gao Huan.
translations.idiomatic: The older brother He Bayong, styled Ani, during Emperor Xiaowu of Wei reached Grand Commandant and was enfeoffed Prince of Yan commandery; he was killed by Gao Huan.

sentences.zh: 岳字阿斗泥。

translations.literal: Bayue, styled Adouni.
translations.idiomatic: He Bayue, styled Adouni.

sentences.zh: 少有大志，愛施好士。

translations.literal: In youth he had great ambition, loved to give and delighted in scholars.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he had great ambition, loved to give, and delighted in scholars.

sentences.zh: 初為太學生，及長，能左右馳射，驍果絕人。

translations.literal: Initially a National University student; when grown, could shoot on horseback to left and right; valor and daring surpassed others.
translations.idiomatic: He was first a National University student; when grown he could shoot on horseback to left and right, and his valor surpassed others.

sentences.zh: 不讀兵書而暗與之合，識者咸異之。

translations.literal: Without reading military books, he tacitly accorded with them; those who knew all marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: Without reading military books, he tacitly accorded with them; those who knew him all marveled.

sentences.zh: 與父兄誅衛可孤之後，廣陽王元深以岳為帳內軍主。

translations.literal: After he and his father and brothers killed Wei Ke'gu, Prince of Guangyang Yuan Shen made Bayue camp-inside army commander.
translations.idiomatic: After he and his father and brothers killed Wei Ke'gu, Prince of Guangyang Yuan Shen made He Bayue camp-inside army commander.

sentences.zh: 又表為強弩將軍。

translations.literal: He also memorialized to make him Powerful Crossbow General.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shen also memorialized to make him Powerful Crossbow General.

sentences.zh: 後與兄勝俱鎮恒州。

translations.literal: Later together with older brother Sheng he garrisoned Heng Province.
translations.idiomatic: Later he and his older brother He Basheng together garrisoned Heng Province.

sentences.zh: 州陷，投爾朱榮。

translations.literal: When the province fell, he joined Erzhu Rong.
translations.idiomatic: When the province fell, he joined Erzhu Rong.

sentences.zh: 榮待之甚厚，以為別將，尋為都督。

translations.literal: Rong treated him very generously, making him Separate General; soon Grand Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Rong treated him very generously, making him Separate General and soon Grand Commander.

sentences.zh: 每居帳下，與計事，多與榮意合，益重之。

translations.literal: Often under his tent in council, mostly accorded with Rong's intent; Rong valued him still more.
translations.idiomatic: Often in council under Erzhu Rong's tent, he mostly accorded with Rong's intent, and Rong valued him still more.

sentences.zh: 榮士馬旣衆，遂與元天穆謀入匡朝廷。

translations.literal: Once Rong's troops and horses were numerous, he then with Yuan Tianmu plotted to enter and restore the court.
translations.idiomatic: Once Erzhu Rong's troops and horses were numerous, he plotted with Yuan Tianmu to enter the capital and restore the court.

sentences.zh: 謂岳曰：「今女主臨朝，政歸近習。

translations.literal: He said to Bayue: "Now a female ruler holds court; government rests with favorites.
translations.idiomatic: He said to He Bayue: "Now a woman holds court and government rests with favorites.

sentences.zh: 盜賊蜂起，海內沸騰，王師屢出，覆亡相繼。

translations.literal: Bandits rise like bees; within the seas boils and seethes; royal armies go out repeatedly and destruction follows in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits swarm; the realm seethes; royal armies go out repeatedly and are destroyed in succession.

sentences.zh: 吾累世受恩，義同休戚。

translations.literal: Our house has received grace for generations; our fates are as one.
translations.idiomatic: Our house has received grace for generations; our fates are bound together.

sentences.zh: 今欲親率士馬，電赴京師，內除君側，外清逆亂。

translations.literal: Now I wish personally to lead troops and horses, lightning-fast to the capital, inward to remove evil at the ruler's side, outward to clear rebellious turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Now I wish personally to lead troops and horses swiftly to the capital, inward to remove evil at the ruler's side and outward to clear rebellious turmoil.

sentences.zh: 取勝之道，計將安出？

translations.literal: The way to victory—what plan will you advance?
translations.idiomatic: The way to victory—what plan do you propose?

sentences.zh: 」岳對曰：「夫立非常之事，必俟非常之人。

translations.literal: " Bayue replied: "To establish an extraordinary affair, one must await an extraordinary man.
translations.idiomatic: " He Bayue replied: "To accomplish an extraordinary deed, one must await an extraordinary man.

sentences.zh: 將軍士馬精強，位任隆重。

translations.literal: General, your troops and horses are elite and strong, your position and commission weighty.
translations.idiomatic: General, your troops and horses are elite and strong, and your position and commission are weighty.

sentences.zh: 若首舉義旗，伐叛匡主，何往而不剋，何向而不摧。

translations.literal: If you first raise the banner of righteousness, punishing rebels and restoring the ruler—where would you go and not conquer, what direction would you strike and not crush?
translations.idiomatic: If you first raise the banner of righteousness to punish rebels and restore the ruler, where would you go and not conquer, what direction would you strike and not crush?

sentences.zh: 古人云：『朝謀不及夕，言發不俟駕』，此之謂矣。

translations.literal: The ancients said: 'Morning counsel does not last to evening; words spoken wait not for the chariot'—this is what is meant.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said, 'Morning counsel does not last to evening; words spoken wait not for the chariot'—this is what is meant.

sentences.zh: 」榮與天穆相顧良久，曰：「卿此言，真丈夫之志也。」

translations.literal: " Rong and Tianmu looked at each other a long while and said: "Your words—truly a great man's resolve."
translations.idiomatic: " Erzhu Rong and Yuan Tianmu looked at each other a long while and said: "Your words are truly a great man's resolve."

sentences.zh: 未幾而魏孝明帝暴崩，榮疑有故，乃舉兵赴洛。

translations.literal: Before long Emperor Xiaoming of Wei died suddenly; Rong suspected cause and thus raised troops to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Emperor Xiaoming of Wei died suddenly; Erzhu Rong suspected foul play and raised troops for Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 配岳甲卒二千為先驅，至河陰。

translations.literal: Assigned Bayue two thousand armored soldiers as vanguard; reached Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: He assigned He Bayue two thousand armored soldiers as vanguard; they reached Heyin.

sentences.zh: 榮旣殺害朝士，時齊神武為榮軍都督，勸榮稱帝，左右多欲同之，榮疑未決。

translations.literal: Once Rong had slain court gentlemen, at the time Gao Huan was Rong's army commander and urged Rong to declare himself emperor; those close by mostly wished the same; Rong wavered undecided.
translations.idiomatic: After Erzhu Rong had slain court gentlemen, Gao Huan was Rong's army commander and urged him to declare himself emperor; those around him mostly agreed; Rong wavered, undecided.

sentences.zh: 岳乃從容進而言曰：「將軍首舉義兵，共除奸逆，功勤未立，逆有此謀，可謂速禍，未見其福。

translations.literal: Bayue then calmly stepped forward and said: "General, you first raised righteous troops jointly to remove traitors; merit not yet established, yet hastily this plan—you may speedily call down disaster and will not see its blessing.
translations.idiomatic: He Bayue then calmly stepped forward and said: "General, you first raised righteous troops to remove traitors; merit is not yet established, yet you hastily entertain this plan—you will speedily call down disaster and will not see its blessing.

sentences.zh: 」榮尋亦自悟，乃尊立孝莊。

translations.literal: " Soon Rong also understood himself and thus installed Emperor Xiaozhuang in honor.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon Erzhu Rong also came to his senses and installed Emperor Xiaozhuang.

sentences.zh: 岳又勸榮誅齊神武以謝天下。

translations.literal: Bayue again urged Rong to execute Gao Huan to appease the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He Bayue again urged Erzhu Rong to execute Gao Huan to appease the realm.

sentences.zh: 左右咸言：「高歡雖復庸疏，言不思難，今四方尚梗，事藉武臣，請舍之，收其後效。

translations.literal: Those close all said: "Though Gao Huan is coarse and shallow and speaks without thinking of difficulties, the four quarters are still obstructed and affairs rely on martial officers—please spare him and gather his later effects.
translations.idiomatic: Those around him all said: "Though Gao Huan is coarse and speaks without thinking of difficulties, the four quarters are still unsettled and affairs rely on martial officers—please spare him and gather his later service.

sentences.zh: 」榮乃止。

translations.literal: " Rong then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " Erzhu Rong then desisted.

sentences.zh: 以定策功，授前將軍、太中大夫，賜爵樊城

translations.literal: For merit in settling the plan, appointed former general and Grand Master of Palace Counsel; granted rank Fancheng
translations.idiomatic: For merit in settling the plan, He Bayue was appointed Former General and Grand Master of Palace Counsel and granted the rank of Fancheng

translations.literal: (Commandery)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: Commandery]

sentences.zh: 〔鄉〕男。

translations.literal: [Township] Baron.
translations.idiomatic: Baron of Fancheng township.

sentences.zh: 復為榮前軍都督，破葛榮於滏口。

translations.literal: Again made Rong's vanguard commander; defeated Ge Rong at Fokou.
translations.idiomatic: He again served as Erzhu Rong's vanguard commander and defeated Ge Rong at Fokou.

sentences.zh: 遷平東將軍、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Transferred to General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 坐事免。

translations.literal: Because of an offense he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Because of an offense he was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 詔尋復之。

translations.literal: An edict soon restored him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict soon restored him.

sentences.zh: 從平元顥，轉左光祿大夫、武衛將軍。

translations.literal: He followed in pacifying Yuan Hao, was transferred to left grand master of splendid happiness and martial guard general.
translations.idiomatic: He followed in pacifying Yuan Hao, was transferred to left grand master of splendid happiness and martial guard general.

sentences.zh: 時万俟醜奴僭稱大號，關中騷動，朝廷深以為憂。

translations.literal: At that time Moqi Chounu presumptuously assumed a great title; Guanzhong was in turmoil, and the court deeply worried.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Moqi Chounu presumptuously assumed a great title; Guanzhong was in turmoil, and the court was deeply alarmed.

sentences.zh: 榮將遣岳討之。

translations.literal: Rong was about to send Yue to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Rong was about to send He Bayue to attack him.

sentences.zh: 岳私謂其兄勝曰：「醜奴擁秦、隴之兵，足為勍敵。

translations.literal: Yue privately told his elder brother Sheng: "Chounu holds the forces of Qin and Long—he is fully a formidable foe.
translations.idiomatic: He Bayue privately told his elder brother He Basheng: "Chounu holds the forces of Qin and Long—he is fully a formidable foe.

sentences.zh: 若岳往而無功，罪責立至；

translations.literal: If Yue goes and achieves nothing, blame and punishment will come at once;
translations.idiomatic: If I go and achieve nothing, blame and punishment will come at once;

sentences.zh: 假令剋定，恐讒愬生焉。

translations.literal: even if we should conquer and settle the matter, I fear slander and accusation will arise.
translations.idiomatic: even if we should conquer and settle the matter, I fear slander and accusation will arise.

sentences.zh: 」勝曰：「汝欲何計自安？

translations.literal: " Sheng said: "What plan do you wish to secure yourself?
translations.idiomatic: " He Basheng said: "What plan do you wish to secure yourself?

sentences.zh: 」岳曰：「請爾朱氏一人為元帥，岳副貳之，則可矣。

translations.literal: " Yue said: "Request one man of the Erzhu clan as commander-in-chief, with Yue as his second—then it can be done.
translations.idiomatic: " He Bayue said: "Request one man of the Erzhu clan as commander-in-chief, with me as his second—then it can be done.

sentences.zh: 」勝然之，乃請于榮。

translations.literal: " Sheng approved, and thereupon made the request of Rong.
translations.idiomatic: " He Basheng approved, and thereupon made the request of Erzhu Rong.

sentences.zh: 榮大悅，乃以天光為使持節、督二雍二岐諸軍事、驃騎大將軍、雍州刺史，以岳為持節、假衛將軍、左大都督，又以征西將軍代郡侯莫陳悅為右〔大〕都督，竝為天光之副以討之。

translations.literal: Rong was greatly pleased; he then made Tianguang commissioner with full credentials, supervisor of military affairs in the two Yong and two Qi regions, grand general of fast cavalry, and governor of Yong Province; made Yue commissioner with credentials, acting guard general, and left grand commander; and also made campaign-west general Houmo Chenyue of Dai commandery right [grand] commander—all as Tianguang's deputies to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Rong was greatly pleased; he then made Erzhu Tianguang commissioner with full credentials, supervisor of military affairs in the two Yong and two Qi regions, grand general of fast cavalry, and governor of Yong Province; made He Bayue commissioner with credentials, acting guard general, and left grand commander; and also made campaign-west general Houmo Chenyue of Dai commandery right grand commander—all as Tianguang's deputies to attack him.

sentences.zh: 時赤水蜀賊，阻兵斷路。

translations.literal: At that time Chishui Shu bandits blocked the road with arms.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Chishui Shu bandits blocked the road with arms.

sentences.zh: 天光之衆，不滿二千。

translations.literal: Tianguang's force was less than two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang's force was less than two thousand.

sentences.zh: 及軍次潼關，天光有難色。

translations.literal: When the army halted at Tong Pass, Tianguang showed a troubled countenance.
translations.idiomatic: When the army halted at Tong Pass, Tianguang showed a troubled countenance.

sentences.zh: 岳曰：「蜀賊草竊而已，公尚遲疑，若遇大敵，將何以戰。

translations.literal: Yue said: "Shu bandits are mere grass-thieves; yet the lord still hesitates—if we meet a great foe, with what will we fight?
translations.idiomatic: He Bayue said: "Shu bandits are mere grass-thieves; yet you still hesitate—if we meet a great foe, with what will we fight?

sentences.zh: 」天光曰：「今日之事，一以相委，公宜為吾制之。

translations.literal: " Tianguang said: "Today's affair I wholly entrust to you; you should take command for me.
translations.idiomatic: " Tianguang said: "Today's affair I wholly entrust to you; you should take command for me.

sentences.zh: 」於是進軍，賊拒戰於渭北，破之，獲馬二千疋，軍威大振。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they advanced; the bandits resisted battle north of the Wei River and were defeated; they captured two thousand horses, and the army's prestige greatly rose.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon they advanced; the bandits resisted battle north of the Wei River and were defeated; they captured two thousand horses, and the army's prestige greatly rose.

sentences.zh: 天光與岳進至雍州，榮又續遣兵至。

translations.literal: Tianguang and Yue advanced to Yong Province; Rong also continued sending troops.
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang and He Bayue advanced to Yong Province; Erzhu Rong also continued sending troops.

sentences.zh: 時醜奴自率大衆圍岐州，遣其大行臺尉遲菩薩、僕射万俟仵同向武功，南渡渭水〔攻趨柵。

translations.literal: At that time Chounu personally led a great host to besiege Qi Province; he sent his grand headquarters Yuchi Pusa and vice director Moqi Wutong toward Wugong, south crossing the Wei River [to attack and rush the stockade.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Chounu personally led a great host to besiege Qi Province; he sent his grand headquarters Yuchi Pusa and vice director Moqi Wutong toward Wugong, south crossing the Wei River to attack and rush the stockade.

sentences.zh: 天光使岳率千騎赴〕援。

translations.literal: Tianguang sent Yue with a thousand horsemen to go to] the relief.
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang sent He Bayue with a thousand horsemen to go to the relief.

sentences.zh: 菩薩攻柵已剋，還岐州。

translations.literal: Pusa had already taken the stockade in attack and returned to Qi Province.
translations.idiomatic: Pusa had already taken the stockade in attack and returned to Qi Province.

sentences.zh: 岳以輕騎八百北渡渭，擒其縣令二人，獲甲首四百，殺掠其民以挑。

translations.literal: Yue with eight hundred light horsemen crossed the Wei northward, captured two of their district magistrates, obtained four hundred armored heads, and killed and plundered their people to provoke.
translations.idiomatic: He Bayue with eight hundred light horsemen crossed the Wei northward, captured two of their district magistrates, obtained four hundred armored heads, and killed and plundered their people to provoke them.

sentences.zh: 菩薩率步騎二萬至渭北。

translations.literal: Pusa led twenty thousand foot and horse to the north bank of the Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Pusa led twenty thousand foot and horse to the north bank of the Wei.

sentences.zh: 岳以輕騎數十與菩薩隔水交言。

translations.literal: Yue with several tens of light horsemen exchanged words with Pusa across the water.
translations.idiomatic: He Bayue with several tens of light horsemen exchanged words with Pusa across the water.

sentences.zh: 岳稱揚國威，菩薩自言強盛，往復數反。

translations.literal: Yue proclaimed the state's might; Pusa spoke of his own strength—back and forth several times.
translations.idiomatic: He Bayue proclaimed the state's might; Pusa spoke of his own strength—back and forth several times.

sentences.zh: 菩薩乃自驕踞，令省事傳語岳。

translations.literal: Pusa then sat himself in arrogant ease and had a clerk transmit words to Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Pusa then sat himself in arrogant ease and had a clerk transmit words to He Bayue.

sentences.zh: 岳怒曰：「我與菩薩言，卿是何人，與我對語？

translations.literal: Yue angrily said: "I speak with Pusa—who are you to converse with me?
translations.idiomatic: He Bayue angrily said: "I speak with Pusa—who are you to converse with me?

sentences.zh: 」省事恃隔水，應答不遜。

translations.literal: " The clerk, relying on the water between them, answered without deference.
translations.idiomatic: " The clerk, relying on the water between them, answered without deference.

sentences.zh: 岳舉弓射之，應弦而倒。

translations.literal: Yue raised his bow and shot him; he fell at the twang of the string.
translations.idiomatic: He Bayue raised his bow and shot him; he fell at the twang of the string.

sentences.zh: 時已逼暮，於是各還。

translations.literal: It was already near dusk; thereupon each side returned.
translations.idiomatic: It was already near dusk; thereupon each side returned.

sentences.zh: 岳密於渭南傍水，分精騎數十為一處，隨地形便置之。

translations.literal: Yue secretly along the south bank of the Wei beside the water divided crack horsemen by several tens to one place, placing them as the terrain allowed.
translations.idiomatic: He Bayue secretly along the south bank of the Wei beside the water divided crack horsemen by several tens to one place, placing them as the terrain allowed.

sentences.zh: 明日，自將百餘騎，隔水與賊相見。

translations.literal: The next day he personally led a hundred-odd horsemen and met the bandits across the water.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he personally led a hundred-odd horsemen and met the bandits across the water.

sentences.zh: 岳漸前進，先所置騎隨岳而進，騎旣漸增，賊不復測其多少。

translations.literal: Yue gradually advanced; the horsemen placed earlier followed Yue in advancing; as the horsemen steadily increased, the bandits could no longer gauge how many there were.
translations.idiomatic: He Bayue gradually advanced; the horsemen placed earlier followed him in advancing; as the horsemen steadily increased, the bandits could no longer gauge how many there were.

sentences.zh: 行二十里許，至水淺可濟之處，岳便馳馬東出，以示奔遁。

translations.literal: Having gone about twenty li, to a place where the water was shallow and could be crossed, Yue then galloped eastward to show flight.
translations.idiomatic: Having gone about twenty li, to a place where the water was shallow and could be crossed, He Bayue then galloped eastward to show flight.

sentences.zh: 賊謂岳走，乃棄步兵，南渡渭水，輕騎追岳。

translations.literal: The bandits thought Yue had fled; they then abandoned the foot soldiers, south crossed the Wei River, and with light horsemen pursued Yue.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits thought He Bayue had fled; they then abandoned the foot soldiers, south crossed the Wei River, and with light horsemen pursued him.

sentences.zh: 岳東行十餘里，依橫岡設伏兵以待之。

translations.literal: Yue went east more than ten li, and along a transverse ridge set ambush troops to await them.
translations.idiomatic: He Bayue went east more than ten li, and along a transverse ridge set ambush troops to await them.

sentences.zh: 賊以路險不得齊進，前後繼至，半度岡東，岳乃回與賊戰，身先士卒，急擊之，賊便退走。

translations.literal: The bandits, because the road was perilous, could not advance together; front and rear arrived in succession; when half had crossed the ridge eastward, Yue then turned back and fought the bandits, himself ahead of the soldiers, pressing the attack urgently; the bandits then retreated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits, because the road was perilous, could not advance together; front and rear arrived in succession; when half had crossed the ridge eastward, He Bayue then turned back and fought the bandits, himself ahead of the soldiers, pressing the attack urgently; the bandits then retreated and fled.

sentences.zh: 岳號令所部，賊下馬者，皆不聽殺。

translations.literal: Yue ordered his command: bandits who dismounted—none were permitted to be killed.
translations.idiomatic: He Bayue ordered his command: bandits who dismounted—none were permitted to be killed.

sentences.zh: 賊顧見之，便悉投馬。

translations.literal: The bandits, seeing this, then all cast off their horses.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits, seeing this, then all cast off their horses.

sentences.zh: 俄而虜獲三千人，馬亦無遺，遂擒菩薩。

translations.literal: Before long they captured three thousand men; not a horse was lost either; they then captured Pusa.
translations.idiomatic: Before long they captured three thousand men; not a horse was lost either; they then captured Pusa.

sentences.zh: 仍渡渭北，降步卒萬餘，竝收其輜重。

translations.literal: They then crossed to the north bank of the Wei; foot soldiers numbering more than ten thousand submitted, and they also collected their baggage train.
translations.idiomatic: They then crossed to the north bank of the Wei; foot soldiers numbering more than ten thousand submitted, and they also collected their baggage train.

sentences.zh: 醜奴尋棄岐州，北走安定，置柵於平亭。

translations.literal: Chounu soon abandoned Qi Province, fled north to Anding, and set stockades at Pingting.
translations.idiomatic: Chounu soon abandoned Qi Province, fled north to Anding, and set stockades at Pingting.

sentences.zh: 天光方自雍至岐，與

translations.literal: Tianguang had just come from Yong to Qi, and with
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang had just come from Yong to Qi, and with

translations.literal: (troops)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: troops]

sentences.zh: 〔岳〕合勢。

translations.literal: [Yue] combined forces.
translations.idiomatic: He Bayue combined forces.

sentences.zh: 軍至汧、渭之間，宣言遠近曰：「今氣候漸熱，非征討之時，待秋涼更圖進取。

translations.literal: The army reached between the Qian and Wei rivers and proclaimed to near and far: "Now the weather is gradually hot—it is not the time for campaigning; wait until autumn coolness and then plan advance and capture.
translations.idiomatic: The army reached between the Qian and Wei rivers and proclaimed to near and far: "Now the weather is gradually hot—it is not the time for campaigning; wait until autumn coolness and then plan advance and capture.

sentences.zh: 」醜奴聞之，遂以為實，分遣諸軍散營農於岐州之北百里細川，使其太尉侯元進領兵五千，據險立柵。

translations.literal: " Chounu heard this and then took it as true; he separately dispatched the armies to scatter and camp for farming in Xichuan a hundred li north of Qi Province, making his grand marshal Hou Yuanjin lead five thousand troops to hold the perilous ground and set stockades.
translations.idiomatic: " Chounu heard this and then took it as true; he separately dispatched the armies to scatter and camp for farming in Xichuan a hundred li north of Qi Province, making his grand marshal Hou Yuanjin lead five thousand troops to hold the perilous ground and set stockades.

sentences.zh: 其千人以下為柵者有數處，且戰且守。

translations.literal: Those with stockades of a thousand men and below numbered several places; they both fought and held.
translations.idiomatic: Those with stockades of a thousand men and below numbered several places; they both fought and held.

sentences.zh: 岳知其勢分，乃密與天光嚴備。

translations.literal: Yue knew their force was divided; he then secretly with Tianguang made strict preparations.
translations.idiomatic: He Bayue knew their force was divided; he then secretly with Tianguang made strict preparations.

sentences.zh: 晡時，潛遣輕騎先行路，於後諸軍盡發。

translations.literal: At the hour of the monkey he secretly sent light horsemen ahead on the road; afterward all the armies fully set out.
translations.idiomatic: At the hour of the monkey he secretly sent light horsemen ahead on the road; afterward all the armies fully set out.

sentences.zh: 昧旦，攻圍元進柵，拔之，剩卽擒元進。

translations.literal: At daybreak they attacked and besieged Yuanjin's stockade, took it, and immediately captured Yuanjin.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak they attacked and besieged Yuanjin's stockade, took it, and immediately captured Yuanjin.

sentences.zh: 諸所俘執皆放之，自餘諸柵悉降。

translations.literal: All those captured and seized were released; the remaining stockades all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: All those captured and seized were released; the remaining stockades all submitted.

sentences.zh: 岳星言徑趣涇州，其刺史俟幾長貴以城降。

translations.literal: Yue by forced march went straight to Jing Province; its governor Qiji Changgui submitted the city.
translations.idiomatic: He Bayue by forced march went straight to Jing Province; its governor Qiji Changgui submitted the city.

sentences.zh: 醜奴乃棄平亭而走，欲向高平。

translations.literal: Chounu then abandoned Pingting and fled, intending to go toward Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: Chounu then abandoned Pingting and fled, intending to go toward Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 岳輕騎急追，明日，及醜奴於平涼之長坑，一戰擒之。

translations.literal: Yue with light horsemen pressed the pursuit; the next day he caught Chounu at Changkeng in Pingliang and captured him in one battle.
translations.idiomatic: He Bayue with light horsemen pressed the pursuit; the next day he caught Chounu at Changkeng in Pingliang and captured him in one battle.

sentences.zh: 高平城中又執蕭寶寅以

translations.literal: In Gaoping city they also seized Xiao Baoyin to
translations.idiomatic: In Gaoping city they also seized Xiao Baoyin to

translations.literal: (return)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: return]

translations.literal: [submit].
translations.idiomatic: submit.

sentences.zh: 賊行臺万俟道洛率衆六千，退保牽屯山。

translations.literal: The bandit grand headquarters Moqi Daoluo led six thousand men, retreated, and held Mount Qiantun.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit grand headquarters Moqi Daoluo led six thousand men, retreated, and held Mount Qiantun.

sentences.zh: 岳攻之。

translations.literal: Yue attacked him.
translations.idiomatic: He Bayue attacked him.

sentences.zh: 道洛敗，率千騎而走，追之不及，遂得入隴，投略陽賊帥王慶雲。

translations.literal: Daoluo was defeated, led a thousand horsemen and fled; pursuit could not overtake him; he then got into Long and threw himself on Lueyang bandit chief Wang Qingyun.
translations.idiomatic: Daoluo was defeated, led a thousand horsemen and fled; pursuit could not overtake him; he then got into Long and threw himself on Lueyang bandit chief Wang Qingyun.

sentences.zh: 慶雲以道洛驍果絕倫，得之甚喜，以為大將軍。

translations.literal: Qingyun, because Daoluo's valor and daring were unmatched, was greatly pleased to obtain him and made him grand general.
translations.idiomatic: Qingyun, because Daoluo's valor and daring were unmatched, was greatly pleased to obtain him and made him grand general.

sentences.zh: 天光又與岳度隴至慶雲所居水洛城。

translations.literal: Tianguang again with Yue crossed Long to Qingyun's dwelling at Shuiluo city.
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang again with He Bayue crossed Long to Qingyun's dwelling at Shuiluo city.

sentences.zh: 慶雲、道洛頻出城拒戰，竝擒之。

translations.literal: Qingyun and Daoluo repeatedly came out of the city to resist battle; both were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Qingyun and Daoluo repeatedly came out of the city to resist battle; both were captured.

sentences.zh: 餘衆皆降，悉坑之，死者萬七千人。

translations.literal: The remaining host all submitted; all were buried alive; the dead numbered seventeen thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining host all submitted; all were buried alive; the dead numbered seventeen thousand men.

sentences.zh: 三秦、河、渭、瓜、涼、鄯州咸來歸款。

translations.literal: The three Qins and He, Wei, Gua, Liang, and Shan provinces all came to submit allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: The three Qins and He, Wei, Gua, Liang, and Shan provinces all came to submit allegiance.

sentences.zh: 賊帥夏州人宿勤明達降於平涼，後復叛，岳又討擒之。

translations.literal: The bandit chief Suqin Mingda of Xia Province submitted at Pingliang; later he rebelled again; Yue again attacked and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit chief Suqin Mingda of Xia Province submitted at Pingliang; later he rebelled again; He Bayue again attacked and captured him.

sentences.zh: 天光雖為元帥，而岳功效居多。

translations.literal: Although Tianguang was commander-in-chief, Yue's achievements and merit were the greater part.
translations.idiomatic: Although Tianguang was commander-in-chief, He Bayue's achievements and merit were the greater part.

sentences.zh: 加車騎將軍，進爵為伯，邑二千戶。

translations.literal: He was added general of chariots and cavalry, advanced in rank to earl, fief two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was added general of chariots and cavalry, advanced in rank to earl, with a fief of two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 尋授都督涇北豳二夏四州諸軍事、涇州刺史，進爵為公。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed supervisor of military affairs in the four provinces of north Jing, Bin, and the two Xia, and governor of Jing Province; he advanced in rank to duke.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed supervisor of military affairs in the four provinces of north Jing, Bin, and the two Xia, and governor of Jing Province; he advanced in rank to duke.

sentences.zh: 天光入洛，使岳行雍州刺史。

translations.literal: When Tianguang entered Luoyang, he had Yue act as governor of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Tianguang entered Luoyang, he had He Bayue act as governor of Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 建明中，拜驃騎大將軍，增邑五百戶。

translations.literal: In the Jianming era he was appointed grand general of fast cavalry; his fief was increased by five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jianming era he was appointed grand general of fast cavalry; his fief was increased by five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 普泰初，除都督二岐東秦三州諸軍事、儀同三司、岐州刺史，進封清水郡公，增邑通前三千戶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Putai he was removed as supervisor of military affairs in the three provinces of the two Qi and east Qin, commissioner third rank, and governor of Qi Province; he advanced to Duke of Qingshui commandery; his fief was increased together with the previous to three thousand households.
